items.title: Tooth-Colored Composite Fillings
items.text: When decay or minor damage strikes, composite fillings provide a discreet, durable fix. These resin-based materials are color-matched to your natural tooth and bonded securely in place—so no one will know you’ve had work done.

items.title: Custom Dental Crowns
items.text: A crown acts like a protective helmet for a compromised tooth. We use high-quality materials like porcelain or zirconia to create crowns that blend beautifully with your surrounding teeth while restoring strength, shape, and stability.

items.title: Dental Bridges
items.text: Missing a tooth? A dental bridge literally “bridges” the gap using adjacent teeth or implants as support. Our bridges are precision-crafted for a secure fit and natural appearance, helping you chew, speak, and smile confidently again.

items.title: Inlays & Onlays
items.text: For teeth that are too damaged for a filling but not quite ready for a full crown, inlays and onlays offer the perfect middle ground. These lab-made restorations preserve more of your natural tooth while providing long-term durability and a seamless look.

Natural-looking results that boost your confidence

faqs.q: What procedures are considered restorative dentistry?
faqs.a: Restorative dentistry includes treatments like fillings, crowns, bridges, inlays, onlays, and dental implants—anything that restores the function and structure of a damaged or missing tooth.

faqs.q: How long do dental restorations last?
faqs.a: With proper care and regular checkups, restorations like crowns and bridges can last 10–15 years or longer. Composite fillings may need replacement sooner depending on wear.

Most dental insurance plans cover restorative procedures that are medically necessary. Our team is happy to review your benefits and help you understand your out-of-pocket costs.

faqs.q: What if I haven’t seen a dentist in years?
faqs.a: You’re not alone—and you’re more than welcome here. We specialize in working with patients who are returning to dental care after time away, with no judgment and a focus on comfort. Want to learn more about the types of dental restorations available? Visit the Cleveland Clinic’s guide to dental restorations.
